Class DropdownMulti<T>

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.AbstractPanelElement<DropdownMulti<T>>
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.DropdownMulti<T>
Type Parameters:
T - selection value type; identity via T.equals()
All Implemented Interfaces:
PanelElement
public final class DropdownMulti<T> extends AbstractPanelElement<DropdownMulti<T>>
Multi-selection dropdown control. Sibling to Dropdown, NOT a subclass — Dropdown is final, and the selection model differs fundamentally (lens over Set rather than over a single nullable T). Honors the "separate primitives" deferral named in Dropdown's class doc.

Lens pattern — Supplier<Set<T>> + toggle Consumer<T>

Same shape as Dropdown's single-select lens, scaled up to a Set: library reads the supplier each frame to render the trigger summary + each row's selected/unselected state; library calls the consumer with the clicked item, and the consumer toggles its own set membership. Library never mutates the consumer's set. Selection identity via T.equals() (matches Set.contains(Object)).

Trigger label

Single-select reused its labelFn for the trigger ("show the label of the current selection"). Multi-select has no single universally-correct trigger text: empty? "N selected"? Comma-joined? Consumers vary. So DropdownMulti.Builder.triggerLabel(Function) is required (not optional) and receives the current Set — consumer decides the summary shape entirely.

Click behavior

  • Trigger click — toggles popover open/closed (same as single-select).
  • Row click — fires the toggle Consumer with that item, popover stays open. Distinguishing feature vs single- select (which closes on row pick). Lets the user toggle multiple items in one popover-open session.
  • Action-row click (Select all / Clear all, when configured) — fires the supplied Runnable, popover stays open. The Runnable does the bulk set op (one call vs N consumer fires).
  • Click outside — not auto-dismissed (matches single-select). Close by clicking the trigger again, or Esc-closes-screen via vanilla.

Visual indicator

Each regular row reserves a left-edge column for a vanilla minecraft:icon/checkmark sprite (9×8). Selected rows render the checkmark + the existing COLOR_SELECTED_OVERLAY highlight; unselected rows render the column empty (preserved width keeps text left-aligned across both states). Action rows skip the checkmark column (they're stateless actions, not toggleable items) and render their label in italic for visual differentiation.

API surface

Set<String> selected = new HashSet<>();

DropdownMulti<String> dd = DropdownMulti.<String>builder()
    .at(0, 0)
    .triggerSize(160, 20)
    .items(List.of("Apple", "Banana", "Cherry", "Date"))
    .label(s -> Component.literal(s))
    .triggerLabel(set -> Component.literal(
        set.isEmpty() ? "None selected" : set.size() + " selected"))
    .selection(() -> selected, item -> {
        if (selected.contains(item)) selected.remove(item);
        else                          selected.add(item);
    })
    .selectAllRow(Component.literal("Select all"),
                  () -> selected.addAll(ALL_ITEMS))
    .clearAllRow(Component.literal("Clear all"),
                 selected::clear)
    .maxVisibleItems(8)
    .build();

Render order discipline

Same constraint as Dropdown — the popover renders via direct ctx.graphics() calls inside the element's render(), so dropdowns must be the LAST element declared in their containing panel. See Dropdown's class doc §"Render order discipline" for the full discussion.

Cross-context applicability

Same as Dropdown: yes for MenuContext + StandaloneContext, no for SlotGroupContext + HudContext.

    • getActiveOverlayBounds

      public int @Nullable [] getActiveOverlayBounds()
      Same active-overlay claim shape as Dropdown. While the popover is open, declares its bounds as an exclusive modal-area so clicks behind it (paint-occluded elements) stay inert.
      Returns:
      [x, y, width, height] of the active overlay region, or null if no overlay is active

    • mouseClicked

      public boolean mouseClicked(double mouseX, double mouseY, int button)
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      Called when the mouse is clicked on this element. The dispatcher hit-tests against the element's bounds before calling this method, so implementations know the click is within bounds.

      Returns true if this element consumed the click (preventing further dispatch to slots or vanilla). The default returns false, so render-only elements (TextLabel, Icon, ItemDisplay) don't need to override it.

      The button parameter is the mouse button: 0=left, 1=right, 2=middle. Core Button only consumes left-click; custom elements can handle any button.

      Parameters:
      mouseX - screen-space mouse X
      mouseY - screen-space mouse Y
      button - mouse button (0=left, 1=right, 2=middle)
      Returns:
      true if consumed, false to let the click fall through

    • notifyClickOutsideOverlay

      public void notifyClickOutsideOverlay(double mouseX, double mouseY)
      Outside-click dismiss — closes the open popover when a click lands outside BOTH the popover and the trigger. The dispatcher calls this on every visible element for a click it didn't route into the element (so it fires even when another element consumed the click). In-trigger clicks (toggle) and in-popover clicks (item toggle / select-all) are handled by mouseClicked(double, double, int), and are no-ops here. Mirrors Dropdown.
      Parameters:
      mouseX - screen-space x of the click that fell outside all claims
      mouseY - screen-space y of the click that fell outside all claims

    • mouseScrolled

      public boolean mouseScrolled(double mouseX, double mouseY, double scrollX, double scrollY)
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      Called when the user scrolls the mouse wheel with the cursor over this element's bounds. The container hit-tests before calling — implementations know the cursor is within bounds.

      Returns true if this element consumed the scroll (preventing further dispatch). Default returns false, so non-scrollable elements (Button, TextLabel, etc.) don't need to override it.

      scrollX / scrollY are the wheel deltas — typically scrollY is non-zero (vertical wheel) and scrollX is zero (horizontal wheel, less common).

      Added in Phase 14d-2 alongside ScrollContainer, the first element that consumes scroll input. Existing elements default false and continue to work unchanged.

      Parameters:
      mouseX - screen-space mouse X
      mouseY - screen-space mouse Y
      scrollX - horizontal wheel delta (typically 0)
      scrollY - vertical wheel delta (positive = up, negative = down)
      Returns:
      true if consumed, false to let the scroll fall through

    • keyPressed

      public boolean keyPressed(int keyCode, int scanCode, int modifiers)
      Keyboard navigation over the regular-item region — the keyboard counterpart to mouseClicked(double, double, int), completing the input model and mirroring Dropdown. Scoped to the OPEN popover (no focus model; a closed dropdown consumes nothing). The pinned action rows stay mouse-only.
      • Up / Down — move the highlighted item; auto-scrolls.
      • Enter / Space — toggle the highlighted item's membership; stays open (the multi-select session continues — the keyboard analog of a row click).
      • Escape — close the popover.
      Parameters:
      keyCode - GLFW key code
      scanCode - platform-specific scan code
      modifiers - GLFW modifier bitfield (shift/ctrl/alt)
      Returns:
      true if consumed, false to let the key fall through
